The tumor cells stain for progesterone receptor protein. See note. Note: In this laboratory, we used this antibody to stain 100 breast carcinomas prepared in the usual way (paraffin sections) and we compared the results with determinations of estrogen receptor by biochemical assay. 91% of tumors that stained with this antibody were positive for estrogen receptors by biochemical assay. 96% of tumors that failed to stain with this antibody were negative for estrogen receptors by biochemical assay. When we compared the results of staining of paraffin sections with the results of staining of frozen sections, the predictive value of a positive result was 97% and the predictive value of a negative result was 95%. In this laboratory, we also compared the results of staining of 100 routinely processed breast carcinomas with determinations of progesterone receptors by a hormone binding assay. Sixty-five percent of tumors that stained with this antibody contained progesterone receptors by the biochemical assay, and 98% of tumors that failed to stain lacked the receptors.
